confidence: CONFIRMED (code path, probe); PROBABLE (trigger needs a 418 without a usable Retry-After, which the Futures docs neither promise nor exclude)
rule: DECISIONS D072 (6), D083 (4); AGENTS.md fail closed / no entry while a position is unprotected
summary: One HTTP 418 without a usable Retry-After closes every REST call of the process for 259200 s (3 days), protective stop, entry cancel, emergency close and listenKey keepalive included, even when the answer body states a ban end two minutes away; the code that would use the body time (D083) ships switched off because rest_gate.ban_end_clock_margin_ms is NOT_CONFIGURED. The deadline is persisted and nothing can clear it.
expected: After a ban whose end the exchange states, the process regains REST shortly after that end, at least for risk-reducing calls.
actual: _body_ban_end returns None when the margin is None, so end = now + 259200 s; check() has no exempt category; restore() re-adopts the deadline after a restart.
impact: A resting entry that fills during the self-imposed ban gets no stop, cannot be cancelled and cannot be emergency-closed by the system for up to 3 days; the user-data stream also dies after the listenKey lapses. Data jobs on the same IP do not hold the gate and can earn the ban. Manual action on Binance is the only remedy.
evidence: binance_ratelimit_gate.py:343-344 'if margin is None or ban_until_epoch_ms is None or retry_after_seconds is not None: return None'; config/binance/binance-limits-v1.toml:17 rate_limit_418_no_retry_after_wait_seconds = 259200; config/execution/execution-limits-v1.toml:80 ban_end_clock_margin_ms = "NOT_CONFIGURED"; probe output: GateRestriction(reason='IP_BAN_418', remaining_seconds=259200); 24 h later place_market_close and place_algo_protective raise RateLimitBanActive retry_after_seconds=172800.
why_tests_miss: Tests pin the ratified behaviour (fallback wait, no exemption, margin off); none asks what happens to a position while the gate is closed for the fallback time.
recommendation: Owner decision: set the clock margin so the body end time is used, and/or lower the 418 fallback, and/or add an audited operator command that clears a ban deadline after checking Binance; look for a Futures Retry-After in the first real 418.
known_prior: KNOWN:D083 / AGENTS.md open owner item (described as a harmless refinement; more severe than recorded)

rule: DECISIONS D072 (6), D081 (Q4: no bypass of a 429/418 pause)
summary: Any 429 met by any caller (also a read or a keepalive), and also an HTTP 400 with code -1003 or -1015, pauses every REST call for 120 s when no Retry-After is present: the protective stop, the entry cancel and the emergency close are refused before sending.
expected: Risk-reducing orders are not delayed by an unrelated call's rate-limit answer (the exchange itself exempts reduce-only / close-position orders from its -1008 throttle); the fallback wait follows the documented one-minute weight window.
actual: gate.check() is the first statement of every signed call and has no exempt category; a 429 on snapshot_positions makes place_algo_protective, place_market_close and cancel_normal_order raise RateLimitPauseActive for 120 s; -1015 (per-account order count) starts the same pause.
impact: A position that fills inside the pause can be without a stop for up to two minutes. Counter-argument: after an IP-weight 429 the exchange would refuse the protective call too and sending while limited leads to a 418, so the decision is doubtful, not plainly wrong.
evidence: binance_usdm.py:895 gate.check(); :901-906 gate.record(...); exchange_errors.py:257-289 (-1003 and -1015 are RATE_LIMITED for every call kind); probe output: 'protective stop 1 s later RAISED RateLimitPauseActive ... retry_after_seconds=120', '[400 -1015] ... gate=(RATE_LIMIT_PAUSE_429, 120)'.
why_tests_miss: The tests assert the refusal as the wanted behaviour.
recommendation: Owner decision: keep the rule, or allow one bounded risk-reducing attempt during a 429 pause (never during a 418); separate -1015 from the IP pause; derive the fallback from the documented window.
known_prior: KNOWN:D081 / 19-OWNER-GAPS.md Q4 (the 400/-1015 trigger and the 120 s vs 60 s window are not in that record)

rule: Supervisor contract: an exhausted retry waits for an explicit request_resync()
summary: request_resync(), the only way out of a halted user-data stream, has no caller in src or scripts. After 7 failed reconnects or 120 s (or a ban, an internal error, a dead task, a listenKey failure) the stream stays UNKNOWN until the process is restarted, and the live loop turns the halt into SAFE_MODE that only the operator leaves.
expected: A halted stream can be recovered without a restart, as the module documents.
actual: grep finds request_resync only in the supervisor's own definition and docstrings.
impact: Availability: on a host with a flaky network every outage longer than about two minutes needs the owner (restart, then leave SAFE_MODE by hand). Fails closed; no direct loss shown.
evidence: grep -rn request_resync src scripts -> only binance_userdata_supervisor.py:14,21,355,405,885; limits reconnect_max_attempts = 7, reconnect_max_delay_seconds = 120 (config/binance/binance-limits-v1.toml:31-32); src/live/feeds.py:26-33 (halt -> SAFE_MODE USER_DATA_STREAM_HALTED).
why_tests_miss: Supervisor tests call request_resync() themselves; no test asserts that the composition has a caller.
recommendation: Wire a caller (the planned /resync_stream at least); consider a slow automatic bounded resync (owner decision).

rule: Router/adapter contract: nothing is silently dropped
summary: Two paths lose one stream frame with a log line only and leave the stream LIVE: an exception inside the SDK receive loop is reported as the connection event 'error', which the supervisor ignores while the socket is open; and the outer except of UserDataAdapter._on_raw_message queues nothing and does not set the overflow flag.
expected: A frame that could not be delivered marks a gap (UNKNOWN, then a REST snapshot), like an overflow.
actual: Log line only; no anomaly item, no overflow flag, no state change.
impact: Small: both need an unexpected exception and the periodic REST reconcile is the authority; it is the one place where the gap machinery does not notice a lost frame.
evidence: binance_common/websocket.py:383-385 (except Exception: logging.error('Error in callback for key ...'); emit 'error'); binance_userdata_supervisor.py:594-598 ('error_on_open_connection_ignored'); binance_userdata.py:835-836 (log.error('userdata.raw_callback_failed')).
reproduction: Code read at the cited lines; no probe.
why_tests_miss: Tests inject parser failures, which are handled, not failures outside the parser.
recommendation: Count such a loss like an overflow so the supervisor resyncs.
